growl.what: A: the old approximation (polysynth saws, resonant low-pass wobbled at 7 Hz = 1/8 triplet, drive, bitcrush, OTT); B: `fmgrowl` (3 operators, feedback, unison 3), FM index wobbled at 1/8 triplet and the vowel swept per beat, per-note rates (r=1/8t, 1/16, 1/8, 1/4), a pitch blip on each note

mod.what: A: a polysynth wobble at one rate for the whole phrase (7 Hz typed by hand); B: the same patch with the rate as a note value and changed per note: 1/8t, 1/16, 1/16, 1/8, 1/4 (the wobble's rhythm is the riff)

vowel.what: A: one band-pass with resonance whose cutoff is swept each beat (a filter sweep); B: the `vowel` formant filter swept oo-oh-ah-eh-ee each beat (three formants, Peterson & Barney): the bass 'talks'

wavetable.what: A: pulse-width modulation, the closest the old engine had; B: `wavetable` on the 'vocal' table, its position swept over half a bar and back (a neuro-style morph)

resample.what: A: the growl phrase played live; B: the same growl printed (muted source) and played back by `sampler`s: its first bar cut into 8 slices re-sequenced as 16ths, and its second bar reversed and pitched down a fifth and an octave at the end of the phrase

multiband.what: A: one distortion over the whole growl (drive 18 dB, OTT): the low end distorts with the top; B: `multiband`: below 150 Hz compressed, clean and mono; 150 Hz-2.5 kHz folded and OTT; above 2.5 kHz hard-clipped and widened

dist.what: A: the old `drive` (tanh, odd harmonics); B: wavefolder, then asymmetric saturation (even harmonics), then a hard clip

comb.what: A: the old `chorus`; B: a comb tuned to F4 (feedback 0.85, its delay swept every 8th: metallic, 'screech'), then a flanger on the half bar

gatedverb.what: A: the 909 snare into a long reverb; B: the same reverb gated (`gate`: hold 150 ms, release 25 ms)

drop.what: an 8-bar drop. A: the old approximations (polysynth wobble with drive, bitcrush and OTT; kitsnare and handclap; the chops a faster wobble). B: `fmgrowl` with synced per-note mods through `multiband`, `suppress` and `mseq`; `snare909` and `clap909` into a gated reverb; chops by `sampler` from the growl

vocoder.what: colour bass: A a growl on single notes; B the same growl through a `vocoder` whose carrier is Fm7 (F, Ab, C, Eb): its movement now rings as a chord
